bound_names.may: not ruled out by the evidence

semantics.known_world_rule: An omitted field records epistemic lack of knowledge. It is not an enumeration of selected values and cannot decide a predicate that requires that field.

world_choice_quantifiers.world: w is a completion of missing evidence; bounds are sound across the admissible completion set W.
world_choice_quantifiers.choice: j is a feasible complete forwarding choice tuple inside one fixed w; it is not another evidence completion.
world_choice_quantifiers.possible: S_possible(w) = {q: exists j in J(w,q) with success(w,j,q)}. For fixed w, possible success quantifies j existentially.
world_choice_quantifiers.guaranteed: S_guaranteed(w) = {q: J(w,q) is nonempty and for all j in J(w,q), success(w,j,q)}. For fixed w, guaranteed success quantifies j universally.
world_choice_quantifiers.mode_bounds: For each selected mode m, L_m subset of intersection over w of S_m(w), and union over w of S_m(w) subset of U_m. L_m and U_m are evidence bounds for mode m; they are not interchangeable with choice quantifiers.
world_choice_quantifiers.empty_world_set: If no admissible completion or feasible choice is established, prove neither bound; retain the relevant gap.
world_choice_quantifiers.may_overapproximation: may and the resulting upper bound are sound over-approximations. Membership need not be jointly realizable with another may member.

semantics.choice_rule: A choice is an explicit finite set of feasible forwarding tuples inside a fixed evidence world. Existential and universal tests range over complete tuples only.
semantics.empty_universal_rule: An empty feasible choice set proves neither possible nor guaranteed success.

ordered_firstmatch.predicate_bounds: For rule i, must_i and may_i are request sets with must_i subset of may_i.
ordered_firstmatch.rule_attribution_must: rule_must_i = must(predicate_i) intersect intersection over j<i of (U minus may(predicate_j)); this is a sound attribution bound.
ordered_firstmatch.rule_attribution_may: rule_may_i = may(predicate_i) intersect intersection over j<i of (U minus must(predicate_j)); this is a sound attribution bound.
ordered_firstmatch.conditional: For predicate bounds P and continuation bounds X (match) and Y (miss), D=must(P), N=U minus may(P), Q=may(P) minus must(P): lower=D intersect lower(X) union N intersect lower(Y) union Q intersect lower(X) intersect lower(Y); upper=D intersect upper(X) union N intersect upper(Y) union Q intersect (upper(X) union upper(Y)).
ordered_firstmatch.action_bounds: Fold conditional backwards from the default terminal action. Run the fold once per action to obtain must_action and may_action; this preserves proofs when both uncertain continuations have the same action.
ordered_firstmatch.unknown_rule: An unknown predicate contributes must=false and may=true over its known outer scope. It is never compiled to false.
ordered_firstmatch.rule_order: Earlier applicable rules shadow later rules. A rule's action is not a forwarding choice created by predicate uncertainty.

choice_bounds.possible: possible(S,w) iff there exists a nonempty feasible complete choice tuple j in J(w) with success(S,w,j)
choice_bounds.guaranteed: guaranteed(S,w) iff J(w) is nonempty and for every feasible complete choice tuple j in J(w), success(S,w,j)
choice_bounds.correlation: Choice alternatives are tuples keyed by choice_scope and choice_id. Marginal fields must not be cross-producted.

relation_banks.transition: R_next(Q,H2,C2) = exists H: R(Q,H,C) and T(H,H2,C,C2)
relation_banks.rename_rule: Eliminate the previous current bank only after renaming next to current; never eliminate original request identity.
relation_banks.identity_rule: A relation preserves every field not named by a rewrite, including original request identity and untouched context.
relation_banks.nat_rule: NAT is a relation of (original request, current header, scoped choice tuple), not independent original and translated address sets.
relation_banks.reverse_rule: Reverse bindings use the same scoped choice tuple and binding owner; cluster membership alone does not establish replication.

client_aggregation.requested_flow_set: Deduplicate by request_id within each client; a client with no requests is outside both result sets.
client_aggregation.holds: C_holds = Sources minus projection_client(Requests minus Lower)
client_aggregation.open: C_open = Sources minus projection_client(Requests minus Upper)
client_aggregation.holds_equation: holds = sources minus projection_client(requests minus lower)
client_aggregation.open_equation: open = sources minus projection_client(requests minus upper)
client_aggregation.possible_client: C_possible is C_open for the selected mode; it contains a client only when every requested flow is in the upper evidence bound.
client_aggregation.guaranteed_client: C_guaranteed is C_holds for the selected mode; it contains a client only when every requested flow is in the lower evidence bound.
client_aggregation.scope: Aggregation is per client and universal over that client's requested flows. A success for one member cannot satisfy another member.

noncontiguous_mask.meaning: wildcard bits are unconstrained; all other bits must equal base
